context: Marimekko/mosaic chart showing global market share across 5 industries (Electronics, Healthcare, Automotive, Energy, Finance) broken into 4 segments (Enterprise, Consumer, Government, Emerging); column width encodes industry revenue, row height encodes segment share within industry.
first_impression: Clean and well-labeled with a restrained 4-color palette, but segment order shifts across columns making cross-industry comparison of the same segment require active hunting.
what_works: The Tol Bright 4-color palette is perceptually distinct and colorblind-friendly; in-cell labels with name and percentage eliminate the need to cross-reference a legend for larger cells, and the subtitle clearly explains the dual encoding.
what_doesnt: Treemap auto-sorting reorders segments by value within each column, so the same subcategory (e.g. Consumer) sits at a different vertical position in every industry, breaking horizontal scan comparisons; the narrow Finance column produces very small cells (Government 14%, Emerging 11%) with cramped labels near the minimum readable size.
